answer.summary: Both public functions implement byte-identical normalization: strip leading/trailing whitespace, collapse internal runs of whitespace to single spaces, then apply title-casing. src/format_name.py::format_name and src/profile.py::display_name each return " ".join(value.strip().split()).title(). The check in checks/test_profile.py proves their equivalence by asserting format_name("  ada   lovelace ") == display_name("  ada   lovelace ") == "Ada Lovelace", confirming the duplicated logic produces identical output for a representative input. README.md labels this a refactor fixture: the duplication is intentional, and a behavior-preserving refactor would extract the shared expression into one helper, have both public modules delegate to it, and retain the equivalence check.
